name: Peter Hargreaves
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: From his spare bedroom in Bristol, England, Peter Hargreaves and pal Stephan Lansdown founded a financial-services firm in 1981.
Hargreaves was a chartered accountant for businesses like KPMG before starting the company, Hargreaves Lansdown.
He no longer sits on the firm's board, but still owns nearly 20% of the over $190 billion (assets under administration) business.
In 2017 Hargreaves launched Blue Whale, a fund manager for UK investors.
He is also the primary stakeholder at GomSpace, specializing in ground stations for satellite communications
forbes_facts: Hargreaves is reportedly the second biggest financial backer of Brexit, donating more than $4 million to the cause.
Hargreaves owns an Embraer Legacy 500 jet capable of flying from the UK to Dubai.

name: Geoffrey Kwok
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025)
forbes_bio: Geoffrey Kwok is the elder son of the late Walter Kwok, former chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of Hong Kong's largest developers.
Walter died in October 2018 at age 68. He had been ousted as company chairman earlier in 2008 in a feud with his two brothers, Thomas and Raymond.
After his death, Geoffrey and his brother, Jonathan, took over Empire Group Holdings, a property developer that Walter started after he left SHKP.
The brothers inherited Walter's direct stake in SHKP and are named beneficiaries of one-third of five large family trusts held by their grandmother.
In late 2018 Geoffrey joined the SHKP board. He has worked at the company, helping to manage its hotel and serviced apartments in Hong Kong and mainland China.
forbes_facts: His grandmother Kwong Siu-hing is the widow of Sun Hung Kai Properties cofounder Kwok Tak-seng, who died in 1990.
His sister Lesley is a director on the board of Empire Group Holdings.

name: Satyanarayana Chava
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Satyanarayana Chava is the founder and CEO of Laurus Labs, a pharma and biotech company in Hyderabad, in southern India.
Chava worked in the pharma sector for two decades before starting Laurus Labs as an R&D firm in 2005.
Today, the $658 million (revenue) company supplies pharma ingredients for drugs to treat HIV, cancer, asthma and diabetes.
Chava remains passionate about research spending 25% of his time in the labs and getting involved with new products.
forbes_facts: Chava is listed as an inventor, along with others, in 145 patents granted to his company.
In his spare time, Chava enjoys cooking Indian food and sweets.

name: Sol Zakay
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2011-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Brothers Sol and Eddie Zakay are chairman and deputy-chairman of Topland Group, an investment group with a substantial real estate portfolio.
In February 2019, Topland sold the 26 hotels under its Hallmark brand for approximately $325 million (250 million British pounds).
Among its current hotel properties are London's Hilton Brighton Metropole, the luxurious Royal Crescent Hotel in Bath and the Glasgow Hilton.
The Zakay brothers launched Topland in the U.K. in the 1980s. The group also has interests in lending, healthcare and natural resources.

name: Hayes Barnard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Hayes Barnard is cofounder and CEO of GoodLeap, which has helped finance more than $26 billion in loans to homeowners making climate-friendly home upgrades.
GoodLeap runs a point-of-sale app that contractors use to get homeowner loans approved instantly for items like solar panels and water-saving turf.
The firm was valued at $12 billion in a 2021 funding round that raised $800 million from investors including Michael Dell.
A former Oracle exec, Barnard entered the mortgage lending business in 2003 and was an executive at SolarCity before it was bought by Tesla in 2016.
In 2014, Barnard founded nonprofit GivePower, which develops clean water and energy systems in underserved communities across the world.

name: Chao Teng-hsiung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Chao Teng-hsiung started Farglory Land, one of Taiwan's largest real estate developers, in 1978 and is still its largest shareholder.
Farglory Land is the flagship unit of Farglory Group, whose interests include financial and retail services, air-cargo logistics and hospitality.
Chao also controls Farglory FTZ Investment Holding, Farglory Life Insurance and Farglory Hotel.
Eldest son Wen-Chia, also known as Frank, took over as Farglory Land chairman in 2014 amid a corruption scandal involving Chao.
In 2022 a Taipei court sentenced Chao to seven years in prison on bribery and corruption charges on the first trial. The second trial is still ongoing.
forbes_facts: Born into poverty in western Taiwan, Chao moved to Taipei in 1966 and did odd jobs. He saved money to supply cement to construction firms.
Over time he bought property and developed his own projects, starting out with buildings that combined factories and offices.

name: Tom Ford
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Tom Ford is a fashion designer who founded his eponymous brand Tom Ford International in 2005.
He sold his stake in the company, plus a separate fragrance and cosmetics business, to Estée Lauder in a $2.8 billion deal in November 2022.
The deal saw Ford step down as CEO, but he remained the creative visionary of the company until the end of 2023.
Ford was the creative director of Gucci from 1994 to 2005, helping revitalize the brand and grow its revenues twelvefold to $3 billion.
Ford also has a film production company, Fade to Black, that has won several Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations for its films.
forbes_facts: Ford owns homes in Los Angeles, New York, London, Palm Beach and Santa Fe, as well as an art collection featuring works by Andy Warhol.
Ford moved to New York as a teenager and studied art history at New York University, before transferring to Parsons to study architecture.

name: Thomas Steyer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Tom Steyer spent 26 years running hedge fund Farallon Capital; he sold his stake in 2012 and switched his focus to politics and the environment.
The San Francisco resident has spent over $320 million in federal elections since 2010?plus another $340 million on his own presidential campaign in 2020.
He announced a campaign for governor of California in Nov. 2025.
Steyer and his wife, Kat Taylor, have donated tens of millions of dollars to alma maters Stanford and Yale for "advanced energy" research.
Steyer is a passionate advocate of clean energy and founder of the environmental group NextGen Climate and the green-focused investment firm Galvanize.
forbes_facts: Steyer was captain of the soccer team at Yale University.
For years, Steyer wore the same dated red wool plaid tie nearly every work day; he told Forbes he had 8 ties of the same design.

name: Serge Godin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Serge Godin founded Canadian tech firm CGI Group in 1976 at age 26.
One of nine children, Godin started working for his father (who had just a fifth-grade education) at the family's sawmill at age 12.
He studied computer science and got an MBA from Quebec's Université Laval, then worked in consulting before using $5,000 in savings to start CGI.
Godin serves as co-chair of the $12 billion (revenue) company; he was president and CEO until 2006. His daughter, Julie, was appointed executive chair in 2025.
He has overseen more than 100 acquisitions, including the 1998 purchase of Bell Sygma, which nearly doubled the size of the company at the time.
forbes_facts: When his father's uninsured mill burned down, a young Godin worked at a convenience store after school and at a dry cleaner's on Saturdays to help pay the bills.

name: Alfred West Jr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Alfred West oversees SEI, the $2 billion (revenue) financial services firm he founded in 1968.
SEI, which stands for Simulated Environments Inc., first developed a computer program to train loan officers by simulating a lending environment.
West took SEI public in 1981 and branched out into investment advisory and money management.
He retired as CEO in 2022, after more than 50 years at the helm. He's now executive chairman.
forbes_facts: West dreamed of becoming a fighter pilot when he was younger and studied aerospace engineering at Georgia Tech.
He didn't qualify to fly due to poor eyesight, so he got an MBA at Wharton instead and then launched SEI.

name: Marc Lasry
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Marc Lasry and his sister Sonia founded Avenue Capital Management in 1995 with $7 million in funding from friends and family.
The firm manages about $13 billion in assets and focuses on distressed and undervalued securities.
Lasry was born in Morocco and moved to the U.S. at age 7 with his family, sharing a bedroom with his 2 siblings for a decade.
He is a major supporter of the Democratic Party, having raised funds for President Obama and candidate Hilary Clinton in the past.
Lasry reportedly sold a 25% stake in the Milwaukee Bucks in 2023, when the team was valued at $3.5 billion.
forbes_facts: In 2017, his daughter Sophie married Alex Swieca, the son of a cofounder of hedge fund Highbridge Capital.
A comic book collector, Lasry sold a Wonder Woman #1 comic at auction for a record $291,000 in 2016.
